papers.title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Optimization of Graphene Nanoplatelet Dosage for Mechanical Strength of High-Performance Concrete
papers.abstract: Addition of Graphene Nanoplatelets (GNP) in conventional concrete exhibits significant improvements of mechanical properties. However, an excessive quantity of GNP results in agglomeration, raising the challenges of stress transfer mechanism. An optimized proportion of GNP is one of the governing variables in developing HPC. This article presents the development framework and implementation of Machine Learning (ML) for optimization of the GNP dosage and prediction of mechanical properties namely strength of HPC in compression and splitting tensile actions. A total of 400 candidate records were initially assembled from Scopus-indexed publications; after data cleaning and eligibility screening, 250 records were retained for modelling. XGBOOST and Random Forest regressors were compared. The predicted and optimized results were evaluated with experimental evaluation to validate the accuracy and model efficiency. The model provided 0.075% of GNP by weight of cement as the optimum dosage at the predicted strength value of 70.01 MPa and 6.03 MPa in compression and splitting tensile strength respectively. Using SHAP analysis, the decision made by the algorithm was revealed along with the feature extraction process showing the significance of the input variables on the compressive and splitting tensile strength of the HPC specimens. The model performance and validation of the predicted values with the experimental results established the potential of utilization of the ML-assisted optimization of the GNP dosage.

papers.title: Heat Transfer Enhancement in Mixed Convection Hybrid Nanofluid Flow over a Moving Permeable Surface
papers.abstract: Efficient thermal management in moving-surface systems is important for electronic cooling, microfluidic devices, and advanced heat-transfer technologies. Hybrid nanofluids have attracted considerable attention for their potential to enhance heat transfer and energy transport. This study investigates mixed-convection flow and heat transfer of a Cu–TiO₂/water hybrid nanofluid over a moving permeable surface, considering the simultaneous effects of internal heat generation/absorption, thermal radiation, an inclined magnetic field, porous-medium resistance, Joule heating, and velocity slip. The governing partial differential equations are transformed into a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations via similarity transformations and then solved numerically using the MATLAB bvp4c solver. We compare assisting and opposing flow conditions by examining velocity, temperature, streamline patterns, the skin friction coefficient, and the local Nusselt number. The results show that assisting flow accelerates fluid motion, whereas porous-medium resistance and opposing flow reduce velocity. Joule heating and internal heat generation increase the fluid temperature, and lamina-shaped nanoparticles give the highest heat-transfer rate among the particle shapes considered, although the gain over spherical particles is small. Furthermore, increasing the nanoparticle concentration slightly increases the local Nusselt number. These findings provide useful guidelines for the design and optimization of advanced thermal management and energy transport systems

papers.title: Effect of Water Curing, Interval Spraying, and Raffia-frond covering on Compressive Strength Development of Normal-Strength Concrete
papers.abstract: Concrete curing is essential for maintaining moisture conditions required for cement hydration and compressive-strength development. This study evaluated the effects of continuous water curing, interval spraying, and raffia-frond covering on the compressive-strength development of concrete at 7, 14, 21, and 28 days. A 3 × 4 factorial experimental design comprising three curing methods and four curing ages was adopted, with three replicate specimens per treatment combination, giving a total of 36 concrete cubes. Compressive-strength data were analysed using descriptive statistics, two-factor analysis of variance (ANOVA), effect-size analysis, and Tukey HSD post-hoc tests at a 95% confidence level. Compressive strength increased progressively with curing age under all curing methods. At 28 days, continuous water curing produced the highest mean compressive strength (35.05 N/mm²), followed by interval spraying (31.01 N/mm²) and raffia-frond covering (28.01 N/mm²). Two-factor ANOVA revealed significant effects of curing method (F₂,₂₄ = 2294.54, p < 0.001), curing age (F₃,₂₄ = 8698.45, p < 0.001), and curing method × curing age interaction (F₆,₂₄ = 8.60, p < 0.001). Tukey HSD comparisons showed significant differences among curing methods at each curing age (p < 0.05). Within the investigated conditions, continuous water curing produced the greatest compressive-strength development. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate curing methods in concrete construction practice worldwide.

papers.title: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Low-Profile 16-Element Wideband MIMO Antenna Covering 6.4 – 8.4 GHz for Future 6G Mobile Communications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a 16-element wideband MIMO patch antenna module for future upper mid-band 6G mobile and IoT applications. The proposed antenna operates over 6.4 to 8.4 GHz band thus fully covering the 6.425 – 8.4 GHz band that is currently considered for future IMT services. The antenna is implemented on an FR-4 substrate with an overall size of 150 × 70 × 1.6 mm³ making it suitable for integration into compact handheld terminals. A P-shaped radiating element combined with an optimized ground-slot configuration is employed to achieve wide impedance bandwidth and improved MIMO isolation. The simulated and measurement results show that the proposed antenna maintains an impedance bandwidth of approximately 30% while maintaining an isolation better than 15 dB. The measured MIMO performance demonstrates an envelope correlation coefficient below 0.02, diversity gain above 9.99 dB, channel capacity loss below 0.4 bits/s/Hz and acceptable total active reflection coefficient characteristics. The measured impedance, isolation and diversity parameters show the potential of the proposed antenna architecture for further investigation in the high frequency upper mid-band multiport terminal applications.

papers.title: Investigation on the combined effect of wash-out and oscillatory behaviours on plaque development induced by reverse flow under varying side-branch bifurcation angles
papers.abstract: Coronary atherosclerosis preferentially develops at bifurcations due to complex flow, and bifurcation angle (BA) strongly influences local hemodynamics. The left circumflex (LCx) BA affects flow distribution and reverse flow in the left coronary system, but its effect on hemodynamic indices remains unclear. We numerically investigated the effect of the LCx BA on plaque-prone regions using three hemodynamic indices: time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), and helicity. The analysis was conducted using an idealized left coronary bifurcation model with a fixed left anterior descending (LAD) angle of 40° and systematically varied LCx angles (20°–80°) under physiologic pulsatile flow conditions. A P2P1 finite element method has been used to solve the 3-D unsteady incompressible Navier-Stokes equations based on the constitutive equation of a non-Newtonian model. We found that the area of low TAWSS has a maximum plateau for low BAs (< 40°) because stronger reverse flows with higher BAs enhance the wash-out near the bifurcating region of the LCx. This phenomenon has been supported by confirming the existing fact that stronger reverse flow with a higher BA is closely related to a higher helicity due to the higher BA. The present simulations also reveal that the temporal variation of the size of the reverse flow reaches a maximum near the medium BA (∼40°), leading to the maximum OSI value. Based on the simulation results of the present model, it can be said that a medium BA of the LCx (∼40°) is more plaque-prone than a higher BA.
